Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment
1. Being dissatisfied with the award of compensation of Rs.2,90,194/-, the claimant is in this appeal seeking enhancement.
2. The occurrence of the accident and the liability to pay compensation by the Insurer are not in dispute.

The Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the claimant has suffered disability to the extent of 9% even though the Consulting Neurosurgeon who had been examined has stated that claimant had suffered a psycho neurological disability of 25%.

In my view, since the doctor who had treated the claimant had categorically stated that claimant had suffered neurological disability at 25%, it would be appropriate to determine the whole body disability at 25%.
4. The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant as Rs.7,500/-, since there was no evidence to that effect.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.6,500/- for the accident of the year 2011, it would be appropriate to determine the Mr Paramesha vs Maheshwarappa on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146446829/

Since the claimant was aged 24 years and the disability suffered is at 25%, 40% is to be added towards future prospects to determine monthly income of the claimant for awarding compensation towards 'loss of future income' which comes to Rs.9,100/-.

6. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.4,91,400/- (Rs.9,100/- X 12 X '18' X 25%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
7.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.54,394/- towards 'medical expenses', Rs.10,000/- towards 'conveyance charges' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'food and nourishment'.
The same are just and proper and are accordingly affirmed.
8. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and has not awarded any sum towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, it NC: 2024:KHC:51001 would be appropriate to award Rs.75,000/- each under both the heads.
9. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as two months.

Since the claimant was hospitalized for 18 days, it would be appropriate to treat the laid- up period as four months and consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.26,000/- (Rs.6,500/- X 4 months) towards loss of earnings during laid up period.
10. Since there is evidence which clearly states that the claimant has suffered psycho disability to the extent of 25%, it is obvious that the claimant would also suffer marital prospects.
Therefore, it would be appropriate to award Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'marriage prospects'.
Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

Accordingly, the claimant is held entitled for compensation of Rs.8,46,794/- as against Rs.2,90,194/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
14. The other aspects of the Award of the Tribunal remain undisturbed.
15. This appeal is, accordingly, allowed in part.
